Print Parameter Explorer

Load a parameter sheet (.xlsx, fixed template) to plot print settings against Clarity or Stability.

How to use this tool & prepare your file

 Everything runs inside this file, offline – your data never leaves your computer.

1 · Preparing the spreadsheet

  • Use the template, or keep the layout of the week-1 sheet: headers in rows 1–3, one print per row from row 4, columns A–N in this order: S/N · Material · Colour · Layer Height · Temperature · e1 · e2 · v1 · v2 · a1 · a2 · t1 · Clarity · Stability.
  • The data sheet is found by "S/N" in cell A2 (any sheet name). Header texts are checked; a mismatch names the exact cell to fix.
  • Required in every row: S/N, Material, Temperature, e1, v1, a1, t1, Clarity, Stability. A row missing one is skipped and listed with the reason.
  • Blank or "-" is allowed for: Layer Height (read as 2 mm), Colour (read as "unspecified"), e2 / v2 / a2 (read as "not used"). Assumed values are always highlighted and named in captions.
  • Clarity and Stability: whole numbers 1–5 (Grading Metrics sheet). Numbers only in numeric columns; units are mm, °C, mm/s, mm/s², s.
  • Columns right of N, cell colours and other sheets are ignored. One file is loaded at a time.
  • Number prints in the order they were made – the History view assumes S/N order = test order.

2 · The three views

  • B · 2D map – two parameters as X and Y, colour = Clarity or Stability. Every print is shown. Dotted lines join only prints whose other settings are all identical – that is the only place a fair comparison exists. Unconnected points differ from every other print in at least one setting. Prints at the same spot are spread around a "+".
  • D · Clarity vs Stability – every print as a point in its score cell, coloured by a parameter of your choice. Shows which settings reach both scores.
  • E · History – Clarity and Stability in S/N order, with up to two parameters overlaid on their own right-hand axes. Overlay heights are not comparable with the scores – read when things change, not where lines cross. Large overlay markers = that parameter changed; hollow = assumed value.

3 · Top results (History view)

  • Choose how many to call out and how to rank: Clarity, Stability, Combined (sum), or Weakest score then combined (recommended when a print needs both).
  • Ties share a rank and all prints tied at the cut-off are included, so "Top 3" can show more than 3 prints – the tool says how many.
  • Top S/Ns get a band, a rank label and a ring; their full settings are listed in the table under the chart.

4 · Styling

  • Colour scheme for scores and numeric values (presets are checked for colour-blind safety on black; "Custom" lets you pick two ends).
  • Every legend entry has a colour picker and an opacity slider – fade entries to highlight others. History lines also have a line type; fading an overlay also fades its right-hand axis.
  • S/N labels can be switched off (2D map and Clarity vs Stability). "Reset" restores colours, opacity and line types.
  • Text size is set per item – axis titles, tick labels, legend, point labels (S/N and rank labels) – and applies to the graph on screen and to every export. Sizes are px of the 1600 px-wide export layout: on a 16:9 slide 10 px ≈ 6 pt, so use about 24 px (≈ 14 pt) or more for projection. "Default sizes" resets them.
  • All text – page, graphs and exports – is set in Roboto, which is built into the file.

5 · Export

  • Sizes: 16:9 slide in Full HD (1920 × 1080) or 4K (3840 × 2160), and A4 / A3 landscape at 300 dpi for print. The preview on screen has the same 16:9 shape as the slide exports.
  • 16:9 exports fill a standard widescreen slide (13.33 × 7.5 in) exactly: PNGs are tagged 144 / 288 dpi and PDFs use a 960 × 540 pt page. In PowerPoint / Keynote insert the file and it sits edge to edge.
  • PNG (pixels), SVG or PDF (vector). Background black or transparent (transparent keeps light text – for dark slides).
  • The optional caption records view, axes, S/Ns, top results, assumptions and source file; its text size has its own slider.
  • The preview under the export options shows exactly what will be saved – same size, proportions, background (transparent shown on a checkerboard), text sizes and caption – and updates whenever the graph or an export option changes. PNG and SVG are made from this exact picture; the PDF is converted from it.
  • Roboto is embedded in PNG and PDF. SVG embeds it for browsers; design apps that ignore embedded fonts need Roboto installed.

6 · Reading the results honestly

  • Scores are visual 1–5 grades: treat differences of one step with care, and expect repeats of the same settings to vary (e.g. S/N 1–4, different filament reels).
  • When several settings change at once (e.g. S/N 23: six parameters), no graph can tell which one caused the effect.
  • Anything not in the sheet (geometry, reel, nozzle…) is invisible to the tool – note it right of column N so you can explain outliers.
